title: Cerulean Tech VPC onramp constraints and regional compliance sync
summary: Introductory discovery focused on Cerulean's private onboarding constraints: EU data residency, on-prem gateways, and tight egress controls. Discussed VPC peering, private endpoints, transit gateway vs direct connect, and KMS/HSM options. Agreed to run a network workshop and share security docs and a draft infra diagram + preliminary pricing for a small pilot.
topics: Regional data residency (EU) and egress controls
Transit Gateway and Direct Connect options
KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in flight
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Jordan on the account team, with Priya from SE. Can each of you say who you are?
[00:08] Marcus Hale: Marcus here, CTO, Cerulean. We've got a handful of folks on — Elena, Omar, Sophie, Ben — thanks for doing this.
[00:14] Priya Singh: Hi all, Priya, I focus on infra and private deployments. We'll try to map your network constraints to Redwood Private.
[00:20] Elena Ruiz: Elena, security. Short version: EU data residency, SOC 2 alignment, and we need to ensure that no model inference logs leave our VPC unless we explicitly permit it.
[00:28] Omar Nasir: Omar, NetOps. Main ask: we can't open wide internet egress from our subnet; anything must flow via our transit gateway or Direct Connect.
[00:36] Sophie Kim: Sophie, platform. We run a hybrid cluster on-prem and in AWS eu-west-1 primarily.
[00:42] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick agenda — how you want to host (hosted/dedicated/private), network topology options, security controls, and next steps.
[00:51] Marcus Hale: We looked at Redwood Hosted initially but cloud egress and residency made us pause. We're leaning Private — we want the control but not recreate everything.
[01:02] Priya Singh: Totally understandable. There are a few patterns customers use: VPC peering to our Private control plane + PrivateLink endpoints for the data plane, or full on-prem gateways if you need air-gapped. We also support Dedicated pools that give reserved GPU capacity but still route through private endpoints.
[01:22] Elena Ruiz: Two big constraints — encrypted keys must be customer-managed KMS, preferably HSM-backed for some workloads, and audit logs need to land in our S3 with retention 7 years. Is that doable?
[01:33] Marcus Alvarez: We do integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping and we can export audit logs via a private endpoint to your S3. There are retention settings — we'll share specifics.
[01:42] Omar Nasir: Network detail: we use TGW (transit gateway) for east-west. We prefer not to do VPC peering at scale, because it complicates routing. How does Redwood handle TGW attachments?
[01:52] Priya Singh: We can attach via TGW or use VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. Practically, customers who want central routing choose TGW. Our Private offering can present a managed VPC that you attach to, or we can negotiate an L3 peering model — apologies, I mean attachment.
[02:07] Sophie Kim: If you send a diagram that shows the TGW flow and security controls, that will expedite our architecture review.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: We'll do that. A note: some of our docs call it "VPC pairing" in older transcripts — ignore that, it's peering/attachment.
[02:20] Marcus Hale: We also have regulatory constraints — some datasets must not leave eu-west-1. So region placement matters; can Redwood Private be deployed in eu-west-1?
[02:30] Priya Singh: Yes, we have private deployments in eu-west-1. The control plane can be customer-visible in your VPC. For extra caution, we can pin model execution to instances in the same region and prevent cross-region fallback by policy.
[02:45] Elena Ruiz: What about fallbacks? If capacity is constrained, we can't have requests degrade to a US region.
[02:51] Marcus Alvarez: We support routing policies that constrain region fallbacks. You can define a strict policy: only eu-west-1 and a secondary region within EU if desired.
[02:59] Omar Nasir: On egress — we run strict NAT and only allow specific IPs to talk out. Can Redwood work with our egress control model or do we need to allow broad ranges?
[03:07] Priya Singh: For Private, traffic between your VPC and our managed data plane stays over the peered attachment/PrivateLink so no public egress. If you need to reach an external repo (container registry), we can support configuring VPC endpoints or pull proxies in your environment.
[03:22] Jordan Lee: Quick interjection — pricing wise, the Private model includes a base infra fee and then vCPU/GPU usage; Dedicated is about reserved capacity. We'll follow up with a tailored estimate.
[03:33] Sophie Kim: Important: our legal team will ask about ingress of model binaries. Do you allow us to host model artifacts in our S3 and have your runtime pull them into the private subnet?
[03:42] Priya Singh: Yes, customer-hosted model artifacts is a supported pattern: you can contain the artifacts in your S3 and we pull them through the private network attachment under IAM roles that you control.
[03:53] Elena Ruiz: On keys — if we use our KMS and HSM, does Redwood ever hold unwrapped plaintext model tokens or customer keys?
[04:00] Marcus Alvarez: No, we use envelope encryption. The customer KMS performs the root protect. Redwood only has wrapped keys, and HSM integration can be configured so we never see plaintext.
[04:10] Ben Torres: About audit: we need chain-of-custody logs for requests — who asked what and when. Can logs include tokenized prompt content or only metadata?
[04:20] Priya Singh: We can configure different retention and content levels. By default we keep metadata; content redaction or full logging can be set per route. For privacy-sensitive flows we recommend storing only hashes and metadata.
[04:33] Omar Nasir: A network gotcha we've hit before: overlapping CIDR ranges. Do you have guidance on non-overlapping ranges and if you support NAT translation?
[04:42] Priya Singh: We require non-overlapping CIDRs for VPC peering attachments. For TGW attachments there are routing rules but still best practice to avoid overlaps. We can also support SNAT for traffic egress if needed.
[04:55] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about pilot scope — what would you want to validate first?
[05:00] Marcus Hale: Low risk use-case: internal summarization of knowledge base, EU-only. We want to validate latency, routing via TGW, and audit/export to our S3. Timeline: ideally a two-week pilot next month.
[05:12] Priya Singh: That works. Pilot can be one model instance pinned to eu-west-1 with a small dedicated GPU and a private endpoint into your VPC. We'll provision a sandbox VPC or attach to your staging TGW.
[05:25] Sophie Kim: On staging, we prefer Redwood attach to our staging account and not prod. Also need RBAC integration — we use SAML SSO and SCIM.
[05:33] Marcus Alvarez: We have SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC mapping; Redwood supports SAML/SCIM.
[05:40] Elena Ruiz: Can you run a compliance checklist against SOC 2 and produce mapping to our controls?
[05:46] Jordan Lee: Yes — we'll share our SOC 2 and ISO docs and a control mapping spreadsheet.
[05:51] Ben Torres: Any competitors you see in this space?
[05:54] Jordan Lee: Customers sometimes mention Provider X and Y; Provider X has a managed endpoint but limited regional options, Provider Y often requires more engineering to set up the private plane. We'll include a short comparison.
[06:07] Omar Nasir: Quick technical — how do you handle KV cache and warm starts? We have large prompt windows and want low-latency responses.
[06:15] Priya Singh: The runtime handles KV cache in the data plane; with the private deployment we can pin cache servers in your region. There may be mis-transcripts in docs where KV cache is called, uh, "K-V cash" but it's the same.
[06:28] Speaker 5: (laughs) noted.
[06:30] Jordan Lee: Are there any blockers to starting a pilot from your side?
[06:35] Marcus Hale: Approvals: security signoff (Elena) and budgetary (me). Also need legal to review data processing addendum and a network workshop to sign off design.
[06:45] Elena Ruiz: We'll need a detailed threat model for the private attachment, and confirmation that logs can be pushed to our S3 with server-side encryption using our KMS key.
[06:55] Priya Singh: Confirmed — logs to S3 with SSE-KMS OK. We'll send the exact IAM role snippet.
[07:02] Jordan Lee: Great. Let's talk timelines — what's feasible for you for the workshop?
[07:07] Sophie Kim: Next week is tight; the week after works. We can commit two engineers for a 90-minute network workshop.
[07:13] Jordan Lee: We'll aim to schedule the workshop in two weeks. Priya, can you own the infra diagram and workshop materials?
[07:18] Priya Singh: Yep, I'll prepare a draft infra diagram showing TGW attachment, PrivateLink endpoints for control plane, S3 export path, and KMS flow.
[07:25] Marcus Alvarez: For us to approve we'll need an initial cost estimate for pilot and an overview of scaling implications.
[07:32] Jordan Lee: We'll include a pilot estimate and a rough scale-to-prod model.
[07:36] Elena Ruiz: A note on monitoring — we need per-request tracing and token-level cost attribution so we can audit per-team usage. Is that in Console?
[07:44] Priya Singh: Yes, Redwood Console includes token-level cost breakdowns and tracing hooks. For Private we can route telemetry to your observability endpoints too.
[07:55] Omar Nasir: Regarding peering vs PrivateLink: if we go PrivateLink, do we avoid TGW complexity?
[08:01] Priya Singh: PrivateLink is often simpler for a small number of attachments; TGW scales better for multi-VPC topologies. We'll show both options.
[08:10] Ben Torres: Any recommended guardrails for preventing model leakage or accidental export of PII?
[08:16] Priya Singh: Use route-level redaction, store only hashes in logs, configure content filters, and enroll in our quality monitoring to detect regressions.
[08:27] Marcus Hale: Ok, sounds good. Can you recap next steps and owners?
[08:31] Jordan Lee: Sure — to recap: 1) Priya will produce infra diagram, TGW vs PrivateLink options, and an IAM snippet for S3 export. 2) Jordan will send security and SOC 2 docs plus an initial pricing for pilot. 3) Schedule 90-minute network workshop in two weeks. 4) Provide drumbeat on legal DPA and control mapping.
[08:51] Priya Singh: I'll also include a suggested pilot runbook with timelines and success metrics (latency under X ms, audit export validated, region-only routing).
[09:02] Elena Ruiz: Success metrics: all data stays in eu-west-1, logs to our S3 encrypted with our KMS, and no cross-region fallback.
[09:10] Jordan Lee: Noted. Any final questions?
[09:14] Sophie Kim: One small one — can we run a smoke test with small sample data to ensure model pulls and artifact fetching work over PrivateLink?
[09:21] Priya Singh: Yep, pilot includes a smoke test.
[09:25] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with meeting notes and send calendar invites for the network workshop.
[09:31] Marcus Hale: Thanks.
[09:32] Elena Ruiz: Thank you.
[09:33] Jordan Lee: Bye everyone.
